newsitem.title: USA: TWA declines comment on Transaero report.
newsitem.headline: TWA declines comment on Transaero report.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc declined to comment Thursday on reports that Russian airline Transaero and a New Jersey investment group may become its strategic partners.
USAToday reported that privately-held Transaero is seeking to develop with TWA an "air transport system" of joint scheduling, flight and passenger operations, the newspaper said.
The report said it was unclear whether Transaero and the Strategic Capital Group would gain control of the airline, which is 30 percent owned by its employees.
"We have talked to a number of different airlines about a number of different things. When we are ready do business with someone, we will certainly announce it," said TWA spokesman Mark Abels.
Abels declined to comment on the USAToday report that Strategic Capital representatives presented their plan to TWA's board on Tuesday.
Abels also said the airline's search for a chief executive officer continues. TWA discussed the CEO situation at Tuesday's board meeting, but "no announcement came from that meeting," he said.
TWA recently tapped board member Gerald Gitner as vice chairman and acting chief executive to replace outgoing CEO Jeffrey Erickson.
